name: Kansas

agency.name: Kansas Corporation Commission, Conservation Division (permits); Kansas Geological Survey, University of Kansas (public well database built from KCC filings)

form.name: Notice of Intent to Drill (with Form CDP-1 Application for Surface Pit and Form KSONA-1 Surface Owner Notification Act certification)
form.number: KCC Form C-1 (July 2014) with instructions; CDP-1 and KSONA-1 in the same packet
form.notes: Read the packet in full as text (420 KB PDF, 78 KB of text; the file name matches a web-search result for the KCC-hosted copy, and the July 2014 revision date matches that result; I did not re-download it, and the KCC intents page refused a request with HTTP 403, so I did not test the KCC site again). C-1 side one: expected spud date; spot description and footages from section lines; operator license number, name, address, contact; contractor; county, lease, well number, field; prorated/spaced field; target formation(s); nearest lease or unit line; ground elevation; well drilled for (oil, gas, disposal, enhanced recovery, storage, seismic) and well class (infield, pool extension, wildcat); equipment type; OWWO block for re-entries; directional, deviated or horizontal with TVD and bottom-hole location; KCC docket number; water well within a quarter mile and public supply within a mile; depth to fresh and usable water; surface and conductor pipe lengths, Alternate I or II; projected total depth and formation at total depth; water source and DWR permit; cores. Side two: plat with acres attributable to the well. Office-use box: API number, district, effective date, authorization expiry (void if drilling has not begun within 12 months), approver. A C-1 must be approved five days before spud. CDP-1 covers the pit; KSONA-1 certifies notice to the surface owner. No items for bond, fee, H2S, frac, mineral owner, formation tops or a permit number. Injection authorizations (Form U-1), plugging (CP-1) and cathodic protection (CB-1) forms were not read. The KCC may now take intents through its online system, which I could not see.

api_number.n: API_NUMBER in the master list and layer; KCC assigns it on approval ('API # 15-' in the office-use box)

permit_number.n: C-1 has no permit number; the API number is the id. KCC_PERMIT column is empty on all 1,442 permits since 2025

well_name.n: WELL (well number) and LEASE_WELL_NAME in the master list; C-1 asks Lease Name and Well #

lease_name.n: LEASE in the master list, LEASE_NAME in the layer; C-1 asks Lease Name

operator_name.n: ORIG_OPERATOR and CURR_OPERATOR in the master list; OPERATOR_NAME in the layer

operator_id.n: C-1 asks the operator License#; no license number column in the KGS file or layer

operator_type.n: C-1 asks license number, name, address, contact only; licensing application not read

bond.n: No bond item on C-1, CDP-1 or KSONA-1; financial assurance sits with operator licensing (not read)

county.n: COUNTY in the ArcGIS layer; the master-list text file has no county column

district.n: 'District #' in the KCC office-use box of the C-1; not a column in the KGS file or layer

field_pool.n: FIELD (blank on 420 of 1,442 permits since 2025), FIELD_NAME in layer; C-1 asks field and prorated/spaced

surface_latlon.n: LATITUDE, LONGITUDE (NAD27, computed from footages; some GPS); C-1 does not ask coordinates

surface_plss.n: TOWNSHIP, RANGE, SECTION, SPOT, FEET_NORTH, FEET_EAST, FOOT_REF; C-1 asks the same footages

bottom_hole_loc.n: C-1 'Bottom Hole Location' (footages, section, township, range) for directional or horizontal wells

lateral_path.n: Horizontal Mississippi wells attach a plat of the horizontal path; the survey follows with the ACO-1

elevation.n: ELEVATION with ELEV_REF (KB, DF, GL or TOPO estimate); C-1 asks ground surface elevation (feet MSL)

surface_owner.n: KSONA-1 certifies notice to the surface owner (owner name and address if KCC sends it); plat of roads and tanks

well_type.n: STATUS/WELL_TYPE codes: OIL, GAS, EOR, SWD, CATH, WATER, D&A; C-1 'Well Drilled For' and Well Class

work_type.n: No work-type column; API suffix (-0001...) is KGS's workover code, -01xx horizontal. C-1 has an 'If OWWO' block

well_direction.n: CHK_HORIZONTAL flag in the layer (horizontal only); C-1 asks directional, deviated or horizontal yes/no

proposed_depth_md.n: C-1 'Projected Total Depth'; the file's DEPTH is the drilled total depth (blank on 470 of 1,442 recent)

proposed_depth_tvd.n: C-1 'If Yes, true vertical depth' for directional or horizontal wells

lateral_length.n: No lateral-length item on the C-1; only the bottom-hole location and horizontal path plat

target_formation.n: C-1 'Target Formation(s)'; file's PRODUCE_FORM is the producing zone from completion (blank on 807 of 1,442)

formation_tops.n: C-1 asks only 'Formation at Total Depth'; KGS tops file is built from logs after drilling

casing_program.n: Surface pipe planned length, Alternate I or II, conductor pipe length; no production casing

cement_program.n: Only the Alternate I or II choice and the surface-pipe cementing affidavit; no volumes or tops

pressure_control.n: Only a certification that a BOP will be used, for horizontal Mississippi wells without a separate application

h2s.n: No H2S item on the C-1, CDP-1 or KSONA-1

pit_waste.n: Separate Form CDP-1 filed with the C-1: pit type, capacity, liner, chloride, sensitive groundwater area

water.n: C-1: water source for drilling (well, farm pond, other), DWR permit #, depth to fresh and usable water; no volume

fracture_plan.n: No stimulation or frac item on the C-1, CDP-1 or KSONA-1

frac_dates.n: ACO-1 Page Three asks the last fracture date if not filed at FracFocus; not in the well file or lookup

frac_chemicals.n: Over 350,000 gal: ingredients and CAS go to FracFocus or ACO-1 Page Three; the well data has none

frac_additives.n: ACO-1 Page Three asks trade name, supplier and purpose if not filed at FracFocus; none published as data

frac_amounts.n: ACO-1 Page Three asks max percent by mass per ingredient if not at FracFocus; none published as data

spacing_unit.n: C-1: prorated/spaced field yes/no; plat: acres attributable to well; acreage attribution plat in spaced fields

spacing_exception.n: C-1 'KCC DKT #' for a K.A.R. 82-3-103a horizontal application; setback certification; no other exception item

mineral_owner.n: Lessor or mineral owner not asked; horizontal wells attach a leased-acreage description and unitization statement

fee.n: C-1 has no fee line; a $30 KSONA-1 handling fee applies only if KCC notifies the owner; fee schedule not read

notice_hearing.n: KSONA-1 certifies notice to the surface owner; no offset-owner notice or hearing item on the forms

date_received.n: Signature date on the C-1; no filing-date column in the KGS file or layer; KCC search not readable (HTTP 403)

date_approved.n: PERMIT (DD-MON-YYYY) in the master list, PERMIT_DATE in the layer; KGS does not say if filed or approved

date_expires.n: 'This authorization expires', void if drilling not started within 12 months; KGS status 'Expired Intent to Drill'

spud_date.n: SPUD in the master list, SPUD_DATE in the layer; C-1 asks 'Expected Spud Date'

completion_date.n: COMPLETION (master list), COMPLETION_DATE (layer); ACO-1 completion form due within 120 days of spud

status.n: STATUS and STATUS2 in the master list; WELL_CLASS in the layer (Approved Intent to Drill, Spudded, Producing...)

plat_image.n: KGS data page lists scanned intents (with the plat) and other forms from KGS and KCC; CHK_SCAN flag in the layer

form_image.n: KGS data page: 'Scanned ACO-1s, drillers logs, intents, plugging reports' linked from the well record

completion_report.n: Scanned ACO-1 completion forms via the KGS well record; CHK_ACO flag in the layer

logs.n: Wireline log headers, LAS and scanned logs via KGS well pages; CHK_LAS and CHK_SCAN flags in the layer

production_link.n: OIL_KID, OIL_DOR_ID, GAS_KID, GAS_DOR_ID link wells to KGS lease production; IP_OIL, IP_GAS, IP_WATER

sources.name: KGS master list of oil and gas wells, 'All Wells' ks_wells.zip (comma-delimited text, same columns as the KGS file format page)
activity_types: permitted wells (new, workover codes in API suffix)
sources.tested: One HEAD 2026-11-01: HTTP 200, Last-Modified 2026-10-09. Opened the copy an earlier researcher downloaded (44,028,388 bytes; ks_wells.txt 204,980,116 bytes; 519,691 rows, 42 columns): 207,731 rows have a PERMIT date (text DD-MON-YYYY), newest 2026-10-08. Permit rows per year match the KGS well-statistics table exactly: 2023 1,372; 2024 1,260; 2025 749; 2026 693 to Oct 8. By month 2026: Jan 42, Feb 36, Mar 67, Apr 105, May 98, Jun 97, Jul 77, Aug 55, Sep 78, Oct 38. Among 1,442 permits since 2025: KCC_PERMIT empty on all, FIELD blank on 420, DEPTH blank on 470, SPUD blank on 486; 145 plain-API rows are EOR or SWD wells and 130 are cathodic or other service holes; 67 carry an API suffix (-0001 mostly). The file is a snapshot (updated about monthly), so the layer is fresher.

sources.tested: Page read (HTTP 200, 11 KB, tables updated Oct 9, 2026): wells permitted 1,372 (2023), 1,260 (2024), 749 (2025), 693 (2026 to date); horizontal wells permitted 10, 12, 4, 8. sources.name: KCC 'Notices of Intents' search (intents to drill filed in the past 365 days, daily download)
sources.tested: One GET with the web-fetch tool returned HTTP 403 and was not repeated or tried another way. From a search-engine summary of the page (not read by me): the search covers the past 365 days, new intents are posted daily and downloadable about 6 p.m. Central, and the KCC points users to the KGS energy portal as an alternative. Fields and download format unknown.

grade_reason: The KGS layer and master list are free, need no login, answered HTTP 200 from here, hold one row per well with a PERMIT date and a spud date, and are rebuilt nightly (layer) or about monthly (zip); yearly permit counts match KGS's own statistics. It is an A with two honest limits: the file has no work-type column (workovers and horizontals show only in the API suffix and the well type) and KGS does not say whether PERMIT is the filing or the approval date. The KCC's own intents search was blocked (HTTP 403) from here.
producer_plan: Source: the KGS 'Oil and Gas Wells' feature layer (nightly) or, for a no-API fallback, the ks_wells.zip master list (about 44 MB, 205 MB unpacked, 42 columns, a snapshot). From the layer: query where=PERMIT_DATE >= DATE '2023-01-01' with outFields=API_NUMBER,WELL_CLASS,WELL_TYPE,PERMIT_DATE,SPUD_DATE,CHK_HORIZONTAL,COUNTY,STATUS2,returnGeometry=false, in pages of 2,000 by resultOffset (about 4,100 rows since 2023 in the zip, so three requests). From the zip: read ks_wells.txt as comma-separated Latin-1, parse PERMIT as DD-MON-YYYY, drop impossible years. Count by permit month. Bands: new = API without a suffix and a type of oil, gas, dry or unknown; injection = EOR or SWD type (about 10 percent of rows; EOR wells are enhanced-recovery injectors); reentry = API with a suffix -0001 to -0099 (KGS's workover codes; 2 to 5 percent of rows); horizontal = suffix -01xx to -09xx (flag only, not a band); other = CATH (cathodic protection boreholes), WATER, strat and observation holes (about 9 percent) so they do not inflate new-well counts. Exclude status 'Cancelled API Number'. Keep 'Approved Intent to Drill' rows: they are permits not yet drilled (229 of 757 in 2026). Caveats: PERMIT is one date per API, so a re-permit of the same API overwrites; recent months keep growing as KGS keys in intents, so the last two weeks are provisional; the layer drops no rows but statuses change over time (a permit can later show Expired Intent or Plugged), so count by PERMIT_DATE, never by current status. If the KCC's own intents list becomes readable it would give filing dates and the 365-day pending queue, but it returned 403 here.
privacy_notes: The KGS file and layer carry operator names (company names; some small operators may be individuals, not screened), well and lease names, API numbers, coordinates and a free-text COMMENTS column that was not screened for names. No phone numbers, e-mails or street addresses in the columns. The C-1 collects contact name, phone and mailing address, and KSONA-1 collects a surface owner's name and address, but neither is in the KGS data. If operators are named, apply the corporation-only rule.
